title: Threatened species in Australia
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches why species become threatened or endangered; one covers scientific naming and the other how new species form, so no existing point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Threatened species in Australia
card: A threatened species is at risk of dying out. A vulnerable species is likely to become endangered if the threats continue. An endangered species is at a very high risk of dying out in the wild.
Habitat loss is a major threat. Clearing land for farms, cities and roads removes the food and shelter that species need.
Other threats include introduced species, such as foxes and feral cats that eat native animals, disease, and climate change, which alters the conditions species live in.
Australia has one of the world's highest rates of mammal extinction. Many of its native mammals live nowhere else, so when they are lost they are lost from the whole world.
draft.remember: Habitat loss, introduced species, disease and climate change threaten species. Australia has lost many mammals.

a.q: A species of small marsupial is likely to become endangered if its threats continue. How is it best described?
a.why: A vulnerable species is likely to become endangered if threats continue. An extinct species has already died out completely, so it does not fit.
a.clue: The species is at risk, but it has not yet reached the highest level of risk.

b.q: A bushland area near Dubbo is cleared for new farms. A native possum that lived only in that bushland now has far fewer places to live and find food. Which threat does this show?
b.why: Clearing the bushland removed the food and shelter the possum needs, which is habitat loss. The case does not mention a disease, a change in climate or a new predator.
b.clue: What was taken away from the possum?
